metadata.description: Daily routines and time-use data for Indonesia, Australia, Italy, Singapore, Malaysia. Sources: national statistics agencies, OECD, We Are Social/DataReportal, academic studies, TomTom Traffic Index.
metadata.notes: All data points 2022+ except where explicitly noted as historical reference. Values represent averages unless stated otherwise.

dataPoints.context: Blended average across full-time, part-time and self-employed workers. Full-time standard is 40h. Indonesia ranks 135th out of 187 countries.
Indonesian male workers average 42.13 hours per week in 2023.
Indonesian female workers average 36.43 hours per week, reflecting higher share of part-time and unpaid domestic work.
Total annual hours worked per worker in Indonesia.
Typical office work start time is 09:00, though near major cities workers may leave home as early as 05:30 to beat traffic.
Typical office work ends at 17:00. Lunch break 12:00–13:00 is a strong cultural norm.
Standard lunch break 12:00–13:00. On Fridays extended to ~90 min (11:30–13:00) for Jumu'ah prayer.
40% of Indonesian respondents report a daily commute of 15–29 minutes in a 2023 survey of 1,048 consumers.
Average 23 min 20 sec to travel 10 km in Jakarta in 2023 (TomTom Traffic Index), up 40 sec from 2022.
Average Jakartan spent 117 hours driving in rush hours in 2023, up 10h 21min from 2022.
Indonesia averages 6.5–6.7 hours of sleep. 51% of Indonesians sleep less than 7 hours per night (YouGov).
51% of Indonesians sleep less than the recommended 7 hours per night.
Subuh (Fajr) prayer typically around 04:20–04:45 depending on location and season. Wakes a significant portion of the population before sunrise.
Dhuhr (midday) prayer ~12:00. Most companies provide musholla (prayer room). Work pauses for this prayer.
Maghrib prayer at sunset (~18:00). Marks the end of the workday for many and start of evening family time.
Breakfast after morning prayer, typically 06:00–08:00. Common dishes: nasi goreng, bubur ayam, gado-gado.
Lunch 12:00–13:00, communal affair at local warungs. Nasi padang, soto, satay are common.
Dinner typically 18:30–20:00, family-centered meal.
Indonesians spent an average of 7 hours 38 minutes on the internet per day (Q3 2023).
dataPoints.source: We Are Social / DataReportal Digital 2024 Indonesia (Q3 2023 data)

dataPoints.context: Indonesians spent an average of 3 hours 11 minutes on social media per day (2023).
Indonesian users spent an average of 6.05 hours per day on mobile devices in 2023.
Indonesian schools typically start at 07:00. Students in urban areas may leave home 05:30–06:00 due to traffic.
People near big cities leave for work around 05:30 to beat heavy traffic.
Motorcycles are the dominant commute mode in Indonesian cities, weaving through traffic. Public transport (buses, commuter trains) increasingly used in Jakarta.
ABS 2024 TUS: Australians spend 10 hours 43 minutes on personal care (sleep, eating, health, hygiene).
dataPoints.source: ABS How Australians Use Their Time 2024

dataPoints.context: ABS 2024 TUS: Australians spend 8 hours 20 minutes on employment and education activities.
dataPoints.source: ABS How Australians Use Their Time 2024

dataPoints.context: ABS 2024 TUS: Australians spend 4 hours 25 minutes on unpaid domestic work (childcare, elder care, housework, volunteering).
dataPoints.source: ABS How Australians Use Their Time 2024

dataPoints.context: ABS 2024 TUS: Australians spend 5 hours 34 minutes on free time (TV/streaming, socialising, exercise, reading).
dataPoints.source: ABS How Australians Use Their Time 2024

dataPoints.context: ABS 2024 TUS: Women spend an average of 4 hours 53 minutes per day on unpaid work.
dataPoints.source: ABS How Australians Use Their Time 2024

dataPoints.context: ABS 2024 TUS: Men spend an average of 3 hours 52 minutes per day on unpaid work.
dataPoints.source: ABS How Australians Use Their Time 2024

dataPoints.source: ABS How Australians Use Their Time 2024

dataPoints.source: ABS How Australians Use Their Time 2024

dataPoints.source: ABS How Australians Use Their Time 2024

dataPoints.source: ABS How Australians Use Their Time 2024

dataPoints.source: ABS How Australians Use Their Time 2024

dataPoints.source: ABS How Australians Use Their Time 2024

dataPoints.context: Average Australian gets 6.9 hours of sleep per night (December 2024 survey). Research suggests 7-8 hours is common but 71% of Australians struggle with sleep quality.
dataPoints.source: Finder survey Dec 2024 / Bemboka Sleep Report 2023

dataPoints.context: ABS NNPAS 2023–2024: Average sleep efficiency for all adults is 83.7% per night.
dataPoints.source: ABS Measured Physical Activity and Sleep 2023-24

dataPoints.context: 71% of Australians report struggling to get a good night's sleep.
Australians commuting on average 48 minutes per day (McCrindle). Urban city workers average 66 minutes. 32% report 15–29 minutes one-way.
Australian city workers' average commute has reached 66 minutes per day.
Australians aged 16–64 spend 6 hours 14 minutes using the internet each day (2024).
dataPoints.source: We Are Social / DataReportal Digital 2024 Australia

dataPoints.context: Australians spend 1 hour 51 minutes per day on social media (2024). In 2023 it was 2 hours 4 minutes.
dataPoints.source: We Are Social / DataReportal Digital 2024 Australia

dataPoints.context: Most Australians consume breakfast before 08:00. Typical: cereal, toast, coffee (light) or bacon/eggs (hot).
Lunch eaten around 12:00–14:00. Light meal: sandwich or salad. Morning tea 10:30–12:00 is a cultural habit.
Dinner between 18:00–21:00, typically 18:30 based on restaurant booking data (Dimmi). Main meal of day.
dataPoints.source: The Daily Meal / Dimmi restaurant booking data

dataPoints.context: WFH workers do 3h 24min unpaid domestic work vs 2h 26min for office workers — 58 min more per day.
dataPoints.source: ABS How Australians Use Their Time 2024

dataPoints.context: ABS 2024 TUS: 48% of males participated in employment activities on a diary day.
dataPoints.source: ABS How Australians Use Their Time 2024

dataPoints.context: ABS 2024 TUS: 38% of females participated in employment activities on a diary day.
dataPoints.source: ABS How Australians Use Their Time 2024

dataPoints.context: Hours worked by Italian employees on main job in 2023 remained nearly unchanged at ~36 hours.
Blended average (full-time + part-time + self-employed): 30.0 hours per week. Italy ranks among shorter working weeks in OECD.
Italy's latest annual hours worked per worker: 1,734.41 hours in 2023 (up from 1,725.83 in 2022).
Typical office start 09:00. Many businesses follow split-day schedule with long lunch break, especially in smaller towns.
Work end time typically 17:00–18:00. Many offices take a 1–2h lunch break (pausa pranzo).
Average Italian bedtime is 00:35 (12:35 AM). Italy is a notably late-night culture.
dataPoints.source: World Population Review / Average Bedtime by Country

dataPoints.context: Average Italian wake-up time is 07:52. Weekday average 07:25, Saturday 07:54, Sunday 08:27.
Derived from bedtime 00:35 and wake time 07:52 = ~7h 17min. Historical ISTAT (2008-09): 8h 17min — significant decline.
dataPoints.source: Derived from World Population Review data

dataPoints.context: Italians typically have breakfast (colazione) between 07:00 and 09:30. Usually light: espresso + cornetto or toast. 81% have adequate breakfast daily (ISTAT 2022).
Nearly 81% of Italians reported having an adequate breakfast every day (ISTAT 2022).
Lunch (pranzo) typically 13:00–15:00. Considered main meal of the day by most Italians. 73.8% eat lunch at home (ISTAT 2022).
73.8% of Italians eat lunch at home (ISTAT 2022). Strong home-meal culture compared to northern Europe.
Dinner (cena) typically 20:00–22:00 (some sources say up to 22:30). Italy has one of Europe's latest dinner times.
Traditional Italian riposo (afternoon nap) around 14:00–15:00. More common in southern Italy and smaller towns.
Based on DataReportal 2023: Italy had 50.78M internet users (86.1% penetration) at start of 2023.
Italians spend ~2 hours per day on social media. Monthly: 23h on social networks + 11h on instant messaging (March 2023).
dataPoints.source: Hootsuite / We Are Social Italy 2023 / Tun2u.com

dataPoints.context: Italy had 43.90 million social media users in January 2023, equating to 74.5% of total population.
Sunday Mass typically 10:00–11:30. Religious practice structured around Sunday mornings and major feast days.
Aperitivo is a deeply embedded Italian social ritual, typically 18:00–20:00 before dinner. Common Monday-Friday especially in northern cities (Milan, Turin).
Italy gender pay gap was 5.6% in 2022 (mean hourly: men €16.8 vs women €15.9). One of lowest in Europe.
Average paid hours worked per week per employee in Singapore in 2023: 43.6h. Declining from 44.8h in 2017.
Full-time Singaporean employees work an average of 45.4 hours per week.
Majority of Singaporean respondents work 8 hours per working day. Common schedule: 08:30–18:00 with 1h lunch.
Common Singapore office hours start 08:30, with some starting 09:00.
Common Singapore office hours end ~18:00. Many workers stay later due to culture of long hours.
Average commute time in Singapore in 2022: ~47 minutes one-way.
Average Singaporean spends 1 hour 14 minutes commuting to and from work per day.
Average Singaporean spends 1 hour 27 minutes per day doing housework after work.
64% of Singaporeans get 6–7 hours of sleep per night; majority average 6.4 hours. Below 7h NSF recommendation.
Only 1 in 4 (25%) of Singaporeans gets more than 7 hours of sleep each night.
Young Singaporean adults' bedtime: 00:39 (later than UK 23:59). Wake time: 08:42.
Singaporeans spend only 27% of their day on leisure activities (excluding sleep). 60% on work/work-related.
Singaporeans spent on average 7 hours/day on the internet in 2023 — 22 min above global average of 6h 37min.
dataPoints.source: We Are Social / DataReportal Digital 2024 Singapore

dataPoints.context: In 2024, Singaporeans spend 6 hours 49 minutes online daily.
In 2024, Singaporeans spend around 2 hours 14 minutes daily on social media.
dataPoints.source: We Are Social / DataReportal Digital 2024 Singapore

dataPoints.context: Singaporeans spend the longest time on TikTok vs any other app: 33 hours 23 minutes per month.
dataPoints.source: We Are Social Digital 2024 Singapore / OOm

dataPoints.context: 70% of Singapore employees report poor work-life balance due to overwhelming workload (Randstad 2022).
Typical Singaporean office worker has breakfast at ~08:20 (kaya toast + kopi before 09:00 start).
dataPoints.source: Lemon8 / Morning Routines in Singapore blog

dataPoints.context: Lunch at noon is central to Singapore routine — hawker centers and food courts. Peak 12:00–13:30.
Dinner peak 19:00–20:00 (18:00–21:00 range). Supper culture: late meal 22:00–midnight.
Singaporeans actively engage with an average of 6.9 social media platforms each month.
96.9% of Singapore population are internet users; 84.7% are active social media users.
Proportion of employees requiring flexible work arrangements rose from 39.5% (2012) to 53.6% (2022). 84.1% who required FWA received it in 2022.
78% of employees felt burnt out at work. Gen X (83%) and women/caregivers (80%) most affected.
Singapore ranks 4th globally in social media adoption at 88.2% of population.
From 1 January 2023, Malaysia's Employment Act 1955 reduced maximum work hours to 45h/week for all employees.
Malaysia mean hours worked: 44.800 hours in both 2023 and 2024 (CEIC Data).
dataPoints.source: CEIC Data / Labour Force Survey Malaysia

dataPoints.context: Standard Malaysian office: 09:00–18:00, 8h/day, 5 days/week (40h). Lunch break 12:30–14:30.
Malaysians spend an average of 53 minutes stuck in traffic. Car: 39.4 min avg drive. Bus: 41.4 min. Train: 38.7 min.
dataPoints.source: Numbeo Traffic Malaysia / Michael Page Malaysia

dataPoints.context: Average commute in KL: ~41.58 minutes. KL drivers spent 159 hours in rush hour traffic in 2022 (TomTom).
KL drivers spent 159 hours in rush hour traffic in 2022; 75 hours were in traffic congestion.
71% of Malaysian commuters use cars for daily travel.
Malaysian adults get an average of 6.4 hours of sleep — below recommended 7-8 hours. 38% of adults are sleep-deprived (National Health and Morbidity Survey 2023).
dataPoints.source: National Health and Morbidity Survey 2023 / Malay Mail 2024

dataPoints.context: 38% of Malaysian adults were not getting enough sleep (National Health and Morbidity Survey 2023). Urban residents sleep less than rural.
Fajr (Subuh) prayer time in Kuala Lumpur: approximately 06:03. First prayer of the day.
Dhuhr (Zohor) prayer time in KL: ~13:18. Midday prayer during lunch break.
Asr prayer time in KL: ~16:24. Afternoon prayer, mid-afternoon.
Maghrib prayer time in KL: ~19:23. Sunset prayer, marks transition to evening.
Isha prayer time in KL: ~20:32. Night prayer, after which leisure/evening activities.
61.3% of Malaysia's population is Muslim (~19.5M people). Prayer times significantly structure daily routines.
Breakfast eaten from wake-up to 10:30. 89% of Malaysians consume breakfast. Northern zone has highest breakfast consumption.
dataPoints.source: Malaysian Adults Nutrition Survey (MANS) / PMC 2023 Breakfast Practices

dataPoints.context: 89% of Malaysians consume breakfast daily (2023 data). 89.20% from MANS study.
Lunch (mid-day meal): 12:30–14:30. 88.57% of Malaysians consume lunch.
Dinner: 18:00–21:00. 91.97% of Malaysians consume dinner — highest meal consumption rate of the three meals.
74.16% of Malaysian adults eat three meals per day (MANS study).
43% of Malaysian respondents dine out several times per week (survey Dec 2022).
Malaysians spent on average 8 hours 6 minutes online in 2023 — slightly down from previous year.
dataPoints.source: DataReportal / We Are Social Digital 2024 Malaysia

dataPoints.context: By 2024, Malaysians' average online time increased 2.5% to 8 hours 17 minutes per day.
dataPoints.source: DataReportal / We Are Social Digital 2025 Malaysia

dataPoints.context: Malaysians spent average 2 hours 48 minutes daily on social media (Q3 2023). Slight increase from 2h 47min in 2022.
Malaysia had 28.68 million social media users in January 2024, equating to 83.1% of total population.
dataPoints.source: We Are Social / DataReportal Digital 2024 Malaysia

dataPoints.context: In 2022, Malaysians spent 3 hours 11 minutes daily on social media — higher than 2023 (2h 48min). Notable decline.
During Ramadan (87% Muslim population), Sahur (pre-dawn meal) is consumed at ~03:00–03:30 before Fajr. Completely restructures daily routine for ~1 month per year.
Older Australians tend to go to bed earlier and wake earlier. Research shows wake times are earliest during middle adulthood; older adults recalibrate to earlier schedules.
dataPoints.source: PMC Sleep Timing Across Lifespan of Australian Adults (2024)

dataPoints.context: ISTAT's 2022-2023 time use multipurpose survey covered 30,000 households from Dec 2022 – Nov 2023. Includes work-life balance, gender equality, volunteer work, sleep, leisure.
Singaporean teenagers clock about 6.5 hours of sleep per night. ~80% of adolescents get less than NSF-recommended hours.
Standard Malaysian work week is 5 days (Monday-Friday). Some sectors/states may observe Friday-Sunday weekends or work 5.5 days.
Friday Jumu'ah prayer requires extended lunch break: many companies give 90-min break starting 11:30. Significant work pattern disruption every Friday.
WFH workers in Australia do 58 extra minutes of unpaid domestic work per day compared to office workers (3h 24min vs 2h 26min).
dataPoints.source: ABS How Australians Use Their Time 2024

dataPoints.context: 41% of employees in Singapore are considering leaving their current jobs in search of better work-life balance (Randstad 2023).
Australian TikTok users spend 42 hours 13 minutes per month on TikTok — highest of any social app.
dataPoints.source: We Are Social Digital 2024 Australia / Campaign Brief

dataPoints.context: Singapore has a strong 'supper' culture: late meal typically 22:00–midnight. Hawker centres stay open late.
Standard Indonesian work week is 5 days (Mon-Fri). Legal maximum 40h/week for 5-day schedule.
dataPoints.source: Indonesian Labour Law / Ministry of Manpower

dataPoints.context: Indonesian university students typically have 4-6 hours of classes per day, starting at 07:00-08:00. Evening self-study common 19:00-22:00.
Rural Indonesian workers (farmers, fishermen) start at 05:00-06:00, working cooler morning hours before midday heat. Day ends ~13:00.
Isha prayer in Indonesia approximately 19:30. After this prayer many families gather for dinner and family time.
During Ramadan, Iftar (break fast) is at Maghrib sunset (~18:00). Most families gather for Iftar together. Strong social and communal meal.
ABS 2024 TUS: 62% of Australians watch TV or streaming on a typical day, averaging 2h 55min.
dataPoints.source: ABS How Australians Use Their Time 2024

dataPoints.context: Most Australian office workers start between 08:00 and 09:00. Standard 9-to-5 culture, flexible arrangements increasing post-COVID.
ABS 2024 TUS: 23% of young people (15-24) play video or mobile games on a typical day.
dataPoints.source: ABS How Australians Use Their Time 2024

dataPoints.context: Australia has 20.80 million social media identities, equating to 86.5% of adult population (2024).
Australia has 25.21 million internet users, representing 95% of the population (2024).
Italy had 50.78M internet users at start of 2023, with 86.1% internet penetration.
Aperitivo (pre-dinner drinks + snacks) 18:00-20:00 is practiced by majority of working adults in northern Italian cities. Key daily social ritual.
In southern Italy and smaller towns, shops close 13:00-16:00 for riposo (rest). Normal reopening 16:00-20:00.

dataPoints.unit: percent of Italian social media users
dataPoints.context: Facebook used by ~80% of Italian social media users. Instagram leads for Gen Z (16-23). WhatsApp dominant for Millennials and Gen X.
Standard Italian work week: 5 days (Mon-Fri). Maximum 40 ordinary hours/week by law, up to 48h with overtime.
Most Singapore companies operate 5-day week. Legal max 44 hours/week. Singapore introduced right to request flexible work from 2024.
Singapore secondary schools start at 07:30. Early start time is key contributor to sleep deprivation in Singaporean youth.
Malaysian government schools start at 07:30 (morning session). Afternoon session 13:00-18:30. Double-session schools common.
Chinese Malaysian yum cha (dim sum breakfast) typically 07:00-10:00 on weekends. Strong social bonding ritual.
Standard Malaysian lunch break: 1 hour (12:30-13:30). Friday lunch extended ~90 min for Jumu'ah prayer for Muslim workers.
Standard Malaysian work week: 5 days (Mon-Fri). Note: states of Johor, Kedah, Kelantan, Terengganu observe Thu-Fri weekend.
Malaysia internet penetration ~90.1% (2024). Mobile internet primary access method.
